Myths on Clay retells the myths of the Mexica (the Aztecs) in the style of their painted books, the codices. These stories were written down in the 1500s by Nahua scholars and Spanish friars from what elders remembered, and every source tells them a little differently: we always say which one we follow. Nahuatl, the Mexica language, is still spoken today.
Sources: Historia de los mexicanos por sus pinturas (c. 1535); Leyenda de los Soles (1558, Codex Chimalpopoca; trans. John Bierhorst, 1992); Florentine Codex, Books 3 and 7 (Bernardino de Sahagún and Nahua scholars, 1577; trans. Anderson & Dibble); Histoyre du Mechique (c. 1547); Codex Boturini; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Alvarado Tezozómoc, 1609); Diego Durán, Historia de las Indias (1581). Further reading: Miguel León-Portilla, Aztec Thought and Culture; Karl Taube, Aztec and Maya Myths.
Narrated by Matías.
